signals.evidence: Bre'em community: HFC volunteers and community manager report lack of trust in politicians and military; officials promised quiet, secure border but this did not materialize in practice.
Bre'em: Continuous shelter residence due to absence of home safe rooms (ממ"דים); public shelters not designed for extended occupancy.
Bre'em: Farmers report limited number of armored field protection booths (מיגוניות) relative to area size; request for regular food supply.
Bre'em: Lack of protected spaces for educational and social activities; no suitable public space available.
Bre'em: Informal activity began today; request for HFC training and volunteer reinforcement.
Bre'em: Business closure concern (pizzeria); shortage of educators; proposal to fill gap using reserve soldiers.
Goren/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Young people fled; those aged 40+ remained.
Goren/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Many residents lack home safe rooms (ממ"דים); public shelters not in optimal condition; some residents have distant shelters.
Goren/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Increase in calls to emergency hotline 106.
Goren/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Elderly population in distress; difficulty reaching safe rooms; some injured.
Goren/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Need for military presence (soldier-teachers) for public information and reassurance.
Abdon/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Residents not leaving; community coordinator recruiting volunteers for HFC.
Abdon/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Additional armored field protection booths; women's evening and adult activities; informal activity ongoing.
Abdon/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Elderly lack home safe rooms; public shelters distant; unable to reach shelters in time.
Abdon/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Army not telling the truth; residents report distrust.
Liman/Matte Asher, Bre'em: Central distress—lack of activities for children; request for soldier-teacher support.
Liman/Matte Asher, Bre'em: Difficulty protecting farmers' security; known protection gaps in process of being addressed.
Liman/Matte Asher, Bre'em: HFC overall functioning well; request for soldier-teachers.
Granot HaGalil/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Sense of fatigue and erosion (שחיקה) from ongoing situation.

Granot HaGalil/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Community resilience expressed in willingness to enable what is possible without distraction; most population returned; young functioning population; coping discourse; basic youth activity; community readiness unit present; community communication without toxic discourse; good relationship with council and HFC.

Granot HaGalil/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Protection gaps; elderly lack protection; HFC not operating at full capacity; no designated coordinator for elderly and people with disabilities; welfare services not connected to this population.

Even Menahem/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Residents Moshe and Yiron: 'We are mentally ill people living here.' Sense of abandonment, pain seeing families and children, feeling like 'periphery of the periphery.'
Even Menahem/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Significant disruption to daily routines; no spaces for social activities under protection; tourism inactive; agriculture significantly damaged.
Even Menahem/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Significant criticism toward the council.

Even Menahem/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Serious problem with home safe rooms; public shelters in poor maintenance condition; HFC not fully operational; limited number of volunteers; no structured mapping of needs and difficulties.
Even Menahem/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Community involvement and mutual aid when needed.
Mattat/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Community cohesion strengthened significantly; overall sense of security; extensive protection in public space.
Mattat/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Families without home safe rooms; need for sewage infrastructure repair.
Mattat/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Community coordinator working at full capacity; need for decompression activities for children and families.
Batzet/Matte Asher, Bre'em: Community dealing with situation; strong leadership and cooperation among different role-holders.

Batzet/Matte Asher, Bre'em: Beginning to enter emergency routine; activity for young ages; farmers working and people going to work; HFC active with volunteers; soldier-teachers; army education core present.

Batzet/Matte Asher, Bre'em: Shortage of suitable shelters; difficulty operating educational frameworks; workers not arriving; youth substance abuse and alcohol issues discovered; need for light shelter renovation for educational activity.

Psuta, Bre'em: Overall resilience but political instability affecting it; people in emergency routine but more free; workshops and learning centers for essential workers and medical staff; decompression workshops and learning center for high school students; student council activity.

Psuta, Bre'em: 55% of homes without protection; shortage of one shelter not suitable for use; weak volunteer network; clubs for elderly and special needs closed and difficult to visit; loneliness and difficulty reported.

Alkosh/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Population partly agricultural, mostly other professions working outside settlement; general apathy expressed in lack of volunteering for leisure activities and community life; no community cohesion; no motivating leadership for action.
Alkosh/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Approximately 70% have home safe rooms; 10% with underground shelter at home; others use 8 community shelters; 3 shelters require repairs.

Alkosh/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: HFC includes only coordinator with no additional functionaries; limited enrichment activity for children; recommendation to fix sirens and address protection and security gaps.

Horfish, Bre'em: Authority broadcasting resilience and high control in settlement; strong settlement; full emergency routine; private businesses opening; council-related matters showing policy hardening.

Horfish, Bre'em: No activity even in public shelters; 30% without protection but no protection issues in public institutions and spaces; loneliness; frameworks not working for elderly, women, and special populations; everything cancelled or minimal via Zoom.

Kibbutz Ayalon/Matte Asher, Bre'em: Evacuation created dependency among some residents for basic needs such as cleaning, repairs, food; some residents still struggling to return to independent functioning.
Kibbutz Ayalon/Matte Asher, Bre'em: Sense of broken community cohesion following evacuation in Iron Swords war; residents more independent and less engaged in community activities.

Kibbutz Ayalon/Matte Asher, Bre'em: Low level of shelters—old systems, stuffy; no protection in local clinic; need to restore medical/clinic response; uncertainty for essential workers; limited informal education activity due to instructors not returning.
Ya'ara/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Silence in streets, almost no vehicles; those who remained are sheltering; those without safe rooms evacuated independently; those with shelters are sheltering.

Ya'ara/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: No frameworks; informal education for some kindergarten and early elementary children; public shelters too small to contain activity or defense policy does not allow (over 50 people).
Ya'ara/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: HFC attempting population survey but only 5 out of over 250 families; loneliness; fatalism because no one will help evacuate to safe room when needed.
Manot/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Not many people in streets but less tension, less depressing to be there; those spoken with were in elevated mood.

Manot/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: No frameworks and desire for informal education or opening frameworks for kindergarten-elementary in settlement areas; not working except remotely; many mobilized to reserves.

Manot/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: HFC and organizations bringing supplies and services via WhatsApp; caring for each other within family framework; receiving aid from organizations; less fear of approaching them for help compared to closer border communities.

Netu'a/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Almost no resident movement throughout settlement; residents in their homes; minimal movement of agricultural vehicles and almost no residents in public space; short warning time creates fear and people stay near protected space.

Netu'a/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Residents do not want evacuation except parents with children; elderly want to stay home; families in homes trying to live under emergency routine; HFC in contact with residents providing response to weakened populations; resilience exists as long as IDF does its job; formal and informal leadership performing processes building trust with community; internal forces and HFC, rabbi, readiness unit working in good communication.
Shtula/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Families from religious core left; weakening of community resilience.
Shtula/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Anxiety about crisis; burnout of role-holders; resilience not high but internal forces holding settlement; volunteers from outside coming to help.
Shtula/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: Elderly unable to leave home; need for medications and food; informal education—little activity with desire to increase responses.

Shtula/Ma'ale Yosef, Bre'em: HFC team contacting all weakened populations with emphasis on widows and elderly; help bringing medicines and food through coordinated purchases among residents or volunteers.
Arraba al-Aramsha/Matte Asher, Bre'em: No resident movement; murmur about evacuation in Iron Swords war.
Arraba al-Aramsha/Matte Asher, Bre'em: Shelters not providing sufficient response; no activities for children during Ramadan.
Arraba al-Aramsha/Matte Asher, Bre'em: Residents filming during alerts.
Adamit/Matte Asher, Bre'em: Most residents in settlement; readiness unit needs refreshing.

Adamit/Matte Asher, Bre'em: HFC operating toward elderly and special needs; parents with small children without protection; parents exhausted but not using wellbeing services; youth mobilized to help in kibbutz; caring for people in shelters.
Kibbutz Snir/Upper Galilee, Haram: Narrative of resilience; high mutual aid; informal activity especially afternoons in shelters; WhatsApp groups use.

Kibbutz Snir/Upper Galilee, Haram: Shortage of armored field protection booth in expansion neighborhood; no siren coverage; need for soldier-teachers and female soldiers for work with children; elderly difficulty reaching shelters due to 0 alert time and doctor rarely coming.
Kibbutz Snir/Upper Galilee, Haram: Problem—shared military and civilian command; need for separation.
Beit Hillel/Mevuot Hermon, Haram: Expansion residents more hysterical (former Kiryat Shmona residents); no intention to leave.

Beit Hillel/Mevuot Hermon, Haram: Decompression activity—one to one-and-a-half hours; work continuity variable; functional continuity 60%; little activity for elderly; protection gaps in elderly club; youth club without standard protection; children's shelter infrastructure issue; home safe room situation improved significantly; shopping trips to Kiryat Shmona; HFC no chairman; limited volunteer network but operating by sub-teams; decompression activity for elderly; decompression for youth and children.
Beit Hillel/Mevuot Hermon, Haram: Resilience—two psychologists on site.
Dafna/Upper Galilee, Haram: Population coping; informal network operating; no protection gaps.
Dafna/Upper Galilee, Haram: Emergency and resilience team established—urgent need for HFC commander; elderly loneliness issue.
Me'iyyan Baruch/Upper Galilee, Haram: No desire to evacuate; strong community and strong authority; community of elderly and welfare population being treated; disabled population receiving response.

Me'iyyan Baruch/Upper Galilee, Haram: Lack of armored field protection booths at bus station and two at playgrounds; lack of standard protection in informal education network; need for soldier-teachers; economic concern weighing; request to finish mission in Lebanon.
Kibbutz Dan/Upper Galilee, Haram: Strong community coping; using community resources including HFC; providing response to population with disabilities and elderly; informal activity occurring.
Kibbutz Dan/Upper Galilee, Haram: No protection in community buildings; need for shelter renovation for continuous residence; siren addition check.
Mishgav Am/Upper Galilee, Haram: Most not ready to leave; took in six new families; doing activities for children; HFC—four residents; community action; optimal response to elderly.

Mishgav Am/Upper Galilee, Haram: Residents with psychological trauma from war and evacuation; not all understand this will be long; lack of firefighters and HFC team; request for decompression; soldier-teachers as much as possible; protection prioritization; people tired and not sleeping well at night.
Manara/Upper Galilee, Haram: Strong community; decompression activity starting tomorrow; strong HFC; meetings schedule of HFC.

Manara/Upper Galilee, Haram: Significant protection gaps; army education core mission; volunteers; lack of welfare cell—not staffed; elderly no meetings due to lack of public space; difficulty descending stairs; age-based division; need for soldier-teacher reinforcement to prevent volunteer burnout; support for decompression.
Tzabyon/Upper Galilee, Haram: Readiness unit soldier suicide.

Tzabyon/Upper Galilee, Haram: Many decompression activities for children and youth; some tired of alerts and returned to sleeping at home; emphasis on community cohesion and not evacuating; agriculture—shortage of armored field protection booth; old neighborhood—no home safe rooms; only one shelter for whole neighborhood.
Tzabyon/Upper Galilee, Haram: Amazing initiatives in community resilience context; HFC working well; volunteers hosting decompression workshops; false alerts lowering resilience.

Karem Ben Zimra/Meron HaGalil, Haram: No support for parents and children; no community activity; feeling alone in battle; lack of siren coverage across settlement; decompression activity for youth—two hours daily; government bureaucracy; need for soldier-teachers urgently.
Kfar Giladi/Upper Galilee, Haram: Narrative of strong community against state neglect and denial of border settlement status.

Kfar Giladi/Upper Galilee, Haram: Decompression for elderly within protected space; inability to provide response for ages 0-6; significant protection gaps; shelters do not contain all residents without protection.

Kfar Giladi/Upper Galilee, Haram: Volunteer network for elderly; major challenge with bedridden patients without protection ability; increase in calls to community resilience team; youth wandering; worsening of mental health situation; need for narrative and sense that IDF is with us.
Mevuot Hermon - Sha'ar Yishuv, Haram: Student departure; rest in positive spirit.
Mevuot Hermon - Sha'ar Yishuv, Haram: Discourse of resilience; resources and volunteer network exist.

Mevuot Hermon - Sha'ar Yishuv, Haram: Protection gaps; volunteer network not always right people; elderly shelter gaps; unable to always reach protected space; need for airing especially elderly; activity for children, kindergarten, informal education, youth in capsules; feeling flooded with military personnel without coverage.
Ramot Naftali/Mevuot Hermon, Haram: Residents okay; surprise enemy not defeated.

Ramot Naftali/Mevuot Hermon, Haram: Damage to functional continuity—low-dose activity; 30 homes without home safe room; gap in volunteer quantity; wide readiness unit (29); no neighborhood heads—not needed; elderly challenge—protection; difficulty reaching shelter during defense; generator shortage for settlement center; lack of training for readiness unit on 'Noah's box.'

Margeliyot/Mevuot Hermon, Haram: Aging population rooted in ground; discourse of resilience; less mutual responsibility; elderly need airing; moving to protected housing seen as problematic; no informal activities; residents feel like targets; without sense of security, in 10-20 years no residents; barely managing to open kindergarten due to lack of children.

Yir'on/Upper Galilee, Haram: Disrupted life routine; agriculture continuing despite lack of protection; HFC very active—received donation; elderly concern in community; main gap—lack of shelter; welfare department call—economic issues, rent payment delays; informal activity—children and youth; tourism business damage; expectation for continued visits.
Ghajar, Haram: Experience of treading carefully due to security events; shops and groceries open; village empty; people in homes; almost no street movement; tight nights.
Ghajar, Haram: Settlement leadership engaged and assisting.
Ghajar, Haram: One public shelter; no public shelters; second shelter opened; 90% of homes without home safe room or shelter.

Ghajar, Haram: Volunteer unit of 35 volunteers—trained and practiced including fire extinguishing cases; welfare department creating personal contact with population needing help; strengthening psycho-social response for children and adults; utilizing resilience centers and resources.
